turns.input: Sister Mereth gives Nicco a pair of leather boots.
turns.narration: Sister Mereth reaches into her document bag and withdraws a worn pair of leather boots, holding them out to Nicco. She does not release them. Her grey eyes appraise him with the same frank assessment she might give any of her charges. "You'll need proper footwear if you're to be walking these streets," she says. "Those coming from... elsewhere often underestimate how much the cobbles take out of a person." She tucks the boots back into her bag and adjusts her key ring with a small jingle of iron. "You stand before Heartstone as if you belong there. If that proves true, you'll be in my square. I prefer my neighbors capable of keeping up."

turns.narration:
Sister Mereth's grey eyebrows lift slightly, though her tired face shows no particular surprise. "I don't give gifts twice," she says, her voice carrying the flat practicality of someone who has managed scarce resources for years. "Keep them, sell them, or leave them on the street. They aren't coming back to me." She adjusts the document bag slung across her shoulder, the large key ring at her hip chiming softly with the movement. "And if you're determined to be stubborn about it, at least stand somewhere I don't have to watch."

The leather boots remain in her hands, unaccepted—her callused fingers gripping them with the same unhurried patience she might apply to a ledger entry that refuses to balance. Around them, the square carries on with its modest daytime traffic: a woman hauling a damp bundle toward the direction of the White Basin, a laborer taking a shortcut past Heartstone's heavy wooden entrance without looking up at its old stonework. The Coined Lie's painted sign, visible across the way, hangs crooked in the still air.
